findings.title: Fallback target locales are only loaded in set_locale, so non-request code gets inconsistent fallbacks
findings.body: The fallback chain built in config/initializers/i18n.rb is [locale, default_locale, :en], but translate() here only calls load_locale(config.locale). The fallback locales (site default and :en) are loaded only by I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale. Code that sets I18n.locale outside a controller request (Sidekiq jobs such as email, mailers, rake tasks) never loads :en or the site default. A key missing from the user's locale then resolves to 'translation missing' there, while the same key falls back correctly in a web process that happened to serve a request first. Because translate() caches zero-argument results per locale (lines 71-76) and only clears that cache on reload!, the 'translation missing' string can stay cached for the life of that process. Fallback targets should be loaded on demand by translate(), not only in the controller filter.

findings.title: Every translation now reads SiteSetting.default_locale through the fallback backend
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale and allocates a new array each time it is invoked. The i18n Fallbacks backend calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] on each I18n.translate call, not only on a miss. Calls with arguments (count:, interpolation) bypass the LRU cache in translate_accelerator.rb, so they hit this path on every invocation, including in tight render loops. Site setting access is also DB-backed on a cache miss, so translation now depends on the settings store being readable, including during boot, migrations, or asset precompilation, where it previously was not needed. The default locale should be read once per request or cached, not recomputed on every lookup.

findings.title: Locale fallback behaviour change is shipped without any specs
findings.body: This PR replaces Rails' configured i18n fallbacks with a custom FallbackLocaleList (fallback order, on-demand loading via ensure_loaded!), removes config.i18n.fallbacks from three environment files, moves the pluralization include, and adds a new ensure_loaded! path to the I18n accelerator. None of this is covered by a spec. There is no test that a missing key in a user's locale falls back to the site default and then to :en, that fallback targets are loaded, or that the removed environment settings are not needed. Regressions in i18n fallback would only show up in production.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain, which depends on default_locale
findings.body: The LRU cache key is built from key, config.locale and the backend object_id only. Results for zero-argument translations now depend on the fallback chain, which includes SiteSetting.default_locale. If the site's default locale is changed at runtime, cached results that were resolved through the old fallback chain are still returned for that process until it restarts or I18n.reload! is called. Nothing in this diff invalidates the cache on a default_locale change, so the cache can serve stale fallback text after an admin change.
